newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico government to test electric vehicles.
newsitem.headline: Mexico government to test electric vehicles.

text.p: The Mexican government will test electric vehicles with an eye toward reducing air pollution, National Ecological Institute President Gabriel Quadri said on Wednesday.

"Several dozen vehicles will be bought with international financing and will be tested under a very professional and exacting scheme by different government departments," Quadri said at a forum on environmental policy.
His comments came as air pollution in Mexico City on Wednesday forced an emergency plan to be put into effect, forcing private cars off the road for two weekdays rather than the customary one.

Quadri said a call for bids from potential suppliers of electric vehicles would be published in November and tests would begin next year. The National Ecological Institute is a government environmental regulatory body.
President Ernesto Zedillo addressed the forum, stressing that support for environmental protection superseded ideological considerations.
"I call upon all political groups to join together and aim to conserve and protect natural resources, with a view to sustainable development," Zedillo said.
The emergency plan to reduce air pollution also entailed reducing at least 30 percent of industrial activity in the Mexico City area.
City authorities said the plan would continue on Thursday.
